title: Bridge
textLines: You climb the ladder toward the Bridge, the ship groaning around you.
Every rung vibrates beneath your gloves.
By the time you reach the upper deck, your breath comes in shallow gasps, each one tasting of ozone and burnt air.
The Bridge doors hiss open with reluctant effort.
Inside, the room glows with a dim, electric pallor.
Unlike the ruined corridors below, the control panels here still flicker with life—some steady, others spasming with warning lights.
Outside the main viewport: darkness.
Not the absence of light, but the kind that swallows it.
You step closer.
The stars are gone—bent, distorted, pulled into streaks that spiral toward an endless void.
For a moment, it doesn't feel like you're looking at something, but rather, something is looking back.
You tear your gaze away and move to the command console.
Your fingers brush the cracked surface, and the displays surge to life.
SYSTEM ACCESS: BRIDGE COMMAND ONLINE
VESSEL: ARV Genesis Transit
PROJECT: Aequalis – Gravitational Singularity Research Initiative
STATUS: CRITICAL
You scroll through the system logs, scanning what remains intact.
Most files are fragmented, overwritten, but a few entries remain readable.
You open one.
Project Aequalis Internal Log
Purpose: To study the duplication and variance effects observed in quantum transport near singularities.
Note: Proximity to gravitational wells yields measurable divergence between transmitted matter and energy reflections.
Safety Protocol: Maintain distance no closer than 0.004 parsecs from the event horizon.
Keep Primary shields active at all times.
Your stomach twists. You check the readouts.
SHIELD STATUS: OFFLINE
DISTANCE TO SINGULARITY: 0.004 parsecs
TRAJECTORY: Stable approach — projected periapsis: 0.004 parsecs
You whisper, "It's meant to be this close."
The words barely leave your mouth before the deck shudders beneath your boots.
Panels flicker. A deep groan rolls through the hull like distant thunder.
But not without shields.
Without shields, the gravitational waves will tear the hull apart.
Then a ping breaks through the silence.
You look down at the console.
LIFE SIGN DETECTED — ENGINEERING
STATUS: ACTIVE
Someone's alive down there.
You glance toward the intercom panel. It's still functional—barely.
You hesitate. Whoever that is, they might be able to stabilize the core, bring the shields online… or they might be hostile.
You press your hand against the console. The metal is cold, vibrating faintly like the pulse of a dying creature.
You take a breath, steadying yourself, and reach for the intercom switch.
The speaker crackles, feedback whining through the Bridge.
You hear faint breathing on the other end—someone alive, moving, working.
You press transmit.
"Engineering, this is the Bridge," you say, voice steadying as you speak.
"Systems show you've still got power down there. We need shields back online, or the ship's going to tear itself apart."
For a moment, only static answers.
Then—
A voice, faint but distinct, cuts through.
"…Copy that. Working on it."
You freeze.
Something about the tone, the rhythm—it's almost—
— End of Part 1 —

choices.text: Seal the Cargo Hold and eject it
